items.ex: Calculate the average speed.
Compare the two graphs.
Define acceleration.
Describe the motion of the car.
Determine the density of the block.
Explain why the pressure increases.
Identify the independent variable.
Predict what happens when the force increases.
items.exzh: 预测力增大时会发生什么。

items.ex: Sketch a distance–time graph.
items.exzh: 画出距离—时间图的草图。

items.ex: State the unit of force.
Suggest one improvement.
Show that the speed is 5 m/s.
Time is a physical quantity.
Always include a unit.
The SI unit of mass is the kilogram.
items.exzh: 质量的国际单位是千克。

items.ex: Measure the length with a ruler.
Mass is measured in kilograms.
Record the time in seconds.
The volume is 50 cm³.
The instrument has a precision of 1 mm.
Resolution is the smallest change that can be detected.
items.exzh: 分辨率是仪器可检测的最小变 化。

items.ex: Every measurement has uncertainty.
items.exzh: 每次测量都存在不确定度。

items.ex: Parallax can cause a reading error.
Read the scale directly from above to avoid parallax.
items.exzh: 从正上方读数以避免视差。

items.ex: Repeat the measurement three times.
Calculate the mean of the valid results.
items.exzh: 计算有效结果的平均值。

items.ex: The value 9.8 s is anomalous.
Repeated results improve reliability.
An accurate value is close to the true value.
The object is in motion.
The book is at rest.
Motion is relative to a reference point.
items.exzh: 运动相对于参照物描述。

items.ex: The total distance is 200 m.
Displacement includes direction.
Speed tells us how fast an object moves.
items.exzh: 速度表示物体运动得多快。

items.ex: Average speed uses total distance and total time.
items.exzh: 平均速度使用总路程和总时间。

items.ex: Velocity includes direction.
The car moves at constant speed.
Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time.
items.exzh: 加速度是单位时间内速度的变 化。

items.ex: The car decelerates when braking.
The initial velocity is zero.
The final velocity is 12 m/s.
The gradient of a distance– time graph is speed.
items.exzh: 距离—时间图的斜率表示速度。

items.ex: A horizontal line shows constant speed.
A steeper gradient means greater speed.
The object is stationary from 4 s to 6 s.
items.exzh: 物体在4 到6 秒静止。

items.ex: A force can change motion.
Force is measured in newtons.
A push moves the box away.
A pull moves the box towards you.
Friction opposes motion.
Air resistance acts opposite to motion.
items.exzh: 空气阻力方向与运动方向相反。

items.ex: Drag increases with speed.
Gravity pulls objects towards Earth.
Weight is a gravitational force.
On Earth, g is about 9.8 N/kg.
items.exzh: 地球表面g 约为9.8 牛/千克。

items.ex: The table exerts a normal contact force.
items.exzh: 桌面对物体施加支持力。

items.ex: The rope is under tension.
A non-zero resultant force causes acceleration.
Balanced forces give zero resultant force.
Unbalanced forces change motion.
items.exzh: 不平衡力改变运动状态。

items.ex: In free fall, gravity is the only force.
items.exzh: 自由落体中只有重力作用。

items.ex: Terminal velocity occurs when forces are balanced.
items.exzh: 力平衡时达到终端速度。

items.ex: Energy is conserved.
A moving car has a kinetic energy store.
items.exzh: 运动汽车具有动能储存。

items.ex: Kinetic energy depends on mass and speed.
items.exzh: 动能取决于质量和速度。

items.ex: A raised object has gravitational potential energy.
items.exzh: 被举高物体具有重力势能。

items.ex: A stretched spring stores elastic energy.
items.exzh: 拉伸弹簧储存弹性势能。

items.ex: Fuel has a chemical energy store.
Some energy is transferred thermally.
items.exzh: 部分能量以热方式转移。

items.ex: Energy is transferred electrically.
Total energy is conserved.
Work is done when a force moves an object.
Work is measured in joules.
Power is energy transferred per unit time.
items.exzh: 功率是单位时间转移的能量。

items.ex: Power is measured in watts.
Light is the useful energy output of a lamp.
items.exzh: 光是灯泡的有用能量输出。

items.ex: Thermal energy may be wasted.
Efficiency cannot exceed 100%.
Density is mass divided by volume.
items.exzh: 密度等于质量除以体积。

items.ex: Measure the dimensions of a regular object.
Use water displacement for an irregular object.
items.exzh: 不规则物体用排水法测体积。

items.ex: The stone’s volume is found by water displacement.
items.exzh: 石块体积通过排水法测得。

items.ex: The object floats on water.
The object sinks because it is denser than water.
items.exzh: 物体因密度大于水而下沉。

items.ex: Pressure is force per unit area.
items.exzh: 压强是单位面积上的力。

items.ex: A smaller area gives greater pressure.
Pressure is measured in pascals.
Atmospheric pressure acts in all directions.
items.exzh: 大气压强向各个方向作用。

items.ex: Liquid pressure increases with depth.
Upthrust acts upward on an object in a fluid.
items.exzh: 流体中的物体受到向上的浮力。

items.ex: Temperature measures how hot or cold something is.
items.exzh: 温度表示物体冷热程度。

items.ex: Thermal energy transfers from hot to cold.
items.exzh: 热能从高温物体转移到低温物 体。

items.ex: Metals are good thermal conductors.
Convection occurs in fluids.
Infrared radiation transfers energy through a vacuum.
items.exzh: 红外辐射可在真空中传递能量。

items.ex: Water has a high specific heat capacity.
Melting changes a solid into a liquid.
Boiling occurs throughout a liquid.
items.exzh: 沸腾发生在液体内部和表面。

items.ex: Evaporation occurs at the surface.
Condensation changes gas into liquid.
A wave transfers energy.
Light is a transverse wave.
Sound in air is longitudinal.
Greater amplitude means more energy.
Wavelength is measured in metres.
Frequency is measured in hertz.
Period is the time for one complete wave.
items.exzh: 周期是一次完整振动所需时间。

items.ex: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.
Light reflects from a mirror.
Light changes direction when it enters glass.
items.exzh: 光进入玻璃时改变方向。

items.ex: Angles are measured from the normal.
The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Sound needs a medium to travel.
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
items.exzh: 声音不能在真空中传播。

items.ex: An echo is reflected sound.
Charge is measured in coulombs.
Current is the rate of flow of charge.
items.exzh: 电流是电荷流动的速率。

items.ex: Current is measured in amperes.
Potential difference transfers energy per unit charge.
items.exzh: 电势差表示单位电荷转移的能 量。

items.ex: Voltage is measured in volts.
Resistance opposes current.
Current flows in a complete circuit.
items.exzh: 电流在完整电路中流动。

items.ex: Current is the same in a series circuit.
items.exzh: 串联电路中各处电流相同。

items.ex: Potential difference is the same across parallel branches.
items.exzh: 并联支路两端电压相同。

items.ex: Copper is a good conductor.
Plastic is an electrical insulator.
A magnetic field surrounds a magnet.
An electromagnet can be switched on and off.
items.exzh: 电磁铁可以接通和断开。

items.ex: A transformer changes alternating voltage.
An atom has a nucleus and electrons.
items.exzh: 原子由原子核和电子组成。

items.ex: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.
items.exzh: 原子核包含质子和中子。

items.ex: A proton has positive charge.
A neutron has no charge.
An electron has negative charge.
Isotopes have the same proton number.
Radioactive decay is random and spontaneous.
items.exzh: 放射性衰变具有随机性和自发 性。

items.ex: Alpha particles are strongly ionising.
Beta particles are moderately penetrating.
Gamma radiation is highly penetrating.
Half-life is the time for activity to halve.
items.exzh: 半衰期是活度减半所需时间。

items.ex: Earth is a planet.
Planets orbit the Sun.
The Sun’s gravitational field keeps planets in orbit.
items.exzh: 太阳重力场使行星保持轨道运 动。

items.ex: The Sun is a star.
The Milky Way is a galaxy.
A light-year is a unit of distance.
Change the independent variable.
Measure the dependent variable.
Keep control variables constant.
A fair test changes one main factor.
items.exzh: 公平实验只改变一个主要因素。

items.ex: Write a clear experimental method.
List the apparatus needed.
Record each observation.
Enter the result in a table.
The conclusion must use the evidence.
Use data as evidence.
State the risk and how to reduce it.
items.exzh: 写出风险及降低风险的方法。

items.ex: Wear goggles as a safety precaution.
items.exzh: 佩戴护目镜作为安全措施。

items.ex: A valid test answers the stated question.
items.exzh: 有效实验能回答所提出的问题。

items.ex: Use a wide range of values.
Use equal intervals.
